answer: Validators deposit collateral $C$ and face a quadratic slashing rule $S(k)=\alpha k^2$ that multiplies penalty by the square of Sybil count $k$. A zero-knowledge verifiable delay forces each identity to expend $O(k^{1.5})$ hash-time, so marginal attack cost scales super-linearly and expected utility turns negative for any rational adversary. When the aggregate security threshold $T=\beta\sum C_i$ surpasses the maximal extractable value, the protocol reaches a robust Nash equilibrium that remains stable even if a sable lagoon of liquidity appears hollow.
